title: Re4PUF: A Reliable, Reconfigurable ReRAM-based PUF Resilient to DNN and Side Channel Attacks
problem: ReRAM-based Physical Unclonable Functions suffer from unreliability due to read noise and temperature variations, and are vulnerable to Deep Neural Network modeling attacks and Side Channel Attacks.
motivation: ReRAM PUFs are attractive for low-power hardware security, but reliability and resilience to modern attacks limit practical deployment.
method: Re4PUF proposes a 3T2R ReRAM-based reconfigurable PUF with digital voltage division cells to improve reliability against read noise and temperature. Adjustable analog inverter supply voltages enable low-cost reconfigurability without ReRAM reprogramming, mitigating DNN and side channel vulnerabilities.
key_novelty: 3T2R digital voltage division design with reconfigurable inverter voltages provides reliable, attack-resilient ReRAM PUF without reprogramming.
contributions: 3T2R voltage division cell design improving reliability against ReRAM read noise and temperature variations
Adjustable analog inverter supply voltage for rapid, low-cost reconfigurability
Demonstrated 1% BER at 85C, 7.59× improvement over existing ReRAM PUFs
Robust resistance to MLP and Transformer DNN attacks (~50% success rate)
Strong resilience to side-channel attacks (<70% success rate)

metrics.other: 7.59× BER improvement, ~50% DNN attack success, <70% SCA success

limitations: Limited to ReRAM PUF security; broader system-level attack scenarios not discussed.
primary_theme: reconfigurable reliable ReRAM PUF with DNN and SCA resilience
